thread.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thin

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Men, we want dominion. We want rulership; we want to subdue the nations. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion,” and he told them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything under foot.

When you read “after our likeness,” understand it is more than what you look like. At that time everybody was of color, yet God gave a specific people rulership. David shows what the likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is not just appearance; it is being righteous. Christ is black, God is black, and we are made after his image, but the image alone does not bring the dominion. In being righteous we will subdue and have dominion over things.

So the government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It is the only way we are going to get it. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 49:16
precepts.why:
Genesis 5 keeps saying each father “begat sons and daughters,” yet it names specific sons, because those particular children were significant: they birthed prophets. Among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. That is why Noah is named and found perfect: he had siblings, but he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of his time dealing with the daughters of men.

Sirach names the righteous line: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Adam had his righteous child, Seth, born “in his own likeness, after his image,” and Noah had his righteous child, Shem: “Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

And out of Shem's line came us. The line God honoured runs from Adam through Seth to Noah and on through Shem to Israel.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 33:14-15
precepts.why:
“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.” There is always a good side and a bad side.

Genesis 5 shows it. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch.” Wait a minute: didn't Cain have a son named Enoch too? He did. Seth's Enoch “walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,” taken up the way Elijah was, walking with God just as Noah walked with God. You had a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch.

It goes on down the line. Seth's line had Methuselah, who lived “nine hundred sixty and nine years,” the longest of any man, and Lamech, who named his son Noah, “saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed,” the ground cursed when Adam sinned. Cain's line had its own Lamech. Two and two, one against another.

precepts.label: Genesis 4:18
precepts.why:
These are Cain's children: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.” So Cain had a son named Enoch, a descendant named Methusael, and one named Lamech.

Now set that beside Genesis 5, Seth's line: Jared begat Enoch, Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The same names on both sides. It is always two: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.

That is Ecclesiasticus 33 lived out in the generations before the flood: “there are two and two, one against another.” And the righteous line, the one named in Genesis 5, is the line of prophets that led to Noah, “a just man and perfect in his generations.”

classes.title: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.label: Genesis 5:1-3
precepts.why:
“the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Who are the men here? Eve said of Cain that she had gotten a man from the Lord, so the daughters of men are Cain's children. The sons of God came out of Adam's line through Seth. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain's daughters.

Genesis 5 shows why Seth's line is called the sons of God: “In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.” God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.”

Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone is not made in God's image. Seth was, and Abel was, but Cain was not. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he was not God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.

So when the sons of God, made in God's likeness through Seth, took the daughters of Cain, the line that was in God's image mixed with the line that was not. The children “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown”: powerful, famous, fierce fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain. Cain had built a city, and the sons of God began dwelling in it and following his ways, just as the sons of God today dwell in Esau's city and learn his ways.

precepts.label: Luke 3:38
precepts.why:
Luke traces Christ's line all the way back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” There it is written plainly. Adam was the son of God, and that line, Seth's line, were the sons of God of Genesis 6.

Abel was one of them, but Cain killed him. Then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel, and the line of the sons of God continued through him.

So “the sons of God saw the daughters of men” is Seth's line looking upon Cain's daughters. What followed is why “it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth.” The sons of God started to behave like Cain and his daughters, and God said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth”: destroy everything and start over. “The earth also was corrupt before God,” because the sons of God mingled with Cain's children; Cain gained dominion, “and the earth was filled with violence,” just as Cain was violent.

precepts.label: Genesis 17:1
precepts.why:
“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God in that time who were doing wickedness with Cain's daughters, Noah did not. There is always that light shining in the darkness all throughout time.

What does perfect mean, and what does it mean to walk with God? God told Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says Noah walked with God, it does not mean he went on long walks and talks on the beach with God. It means he walked in his ways.

Righteous, perfect and just all mean keeping God's commandments. The commandments that Seth kept, Noah was keeping also, while all flesh around him corrupted its way upon the earth.

precepts.label: Genesis 26:5
precepts.why:
God said of Abraham, “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” That is what it means to walk before God and be perfect.

Abraham kept the laws, statutes and commandments just as Noah did. “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God”: he kept the commandments that Seth kept, and that is why he found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the rest of the earth was corrupt and filled with violence.

So the law was not new at Sinai. Noah kept it, Abraham kept it, and those who keep it are the ones God preserves when “The end of all flesh is come before me.”

precepts.label: Revelation 3:7
precepts.why:
Genesis 7 ends with four words: “and the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close that door; God did. Revelation 3:7 shows who holds that power: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.” That is Christ, the one “that hath the key of David.”

Why did God close the door himself? Because of what Noah would hear outside. Noah was a man, and a man has a soft spot. There were babies out there, people begging for their babies, screaming and crying. Noah's own kin were out there too, his siblings and relatives, crying out, why are you doing this? If the door were left to Noah, he might have opened it. So God said, get back, I'll close the door. Noah had to sit inside and hear the screaming, the crying and the begging until there was nothing to hear anymore. That is a terrible thing to live through.

The door was shut only after a long season of mercy. Noah was a hundred years building that boat, and the people were warned the whole time: repent, stop following Cain, keep these laws. They said, we good. God was longsuffering with them. Noah was found righteous “in this generation” because he kept the commandments; that is how he knew the clean beasts from the unclean and how he walked with God. When the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened, only the eight souls on that boat lived.

It is the same today. Right now the door of repentance is open, and Christ is longsuffering with our people. This is the time to get it right. Once that door is closed, that is it; no one can open it, the way the great gulf is fixed. As it was in the days of Noah, so it is now.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 10:3
precepts.why:
Isaac told Esau, “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother.” That goes right back to Cain being a fugitive and a vagabond: wandering all around, in lands that don't belong to him, acquiring them by the sword, killing and massacring and holding himself unaccountable. Some say they did not steal the Native Americans' land, they conquered it. What is the difference? After you conquered it, did you give it back? You kept it and gave it to your children, and then gave land to the Irish and British who came afterward and conquered nothing. That is stealing.

“and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”: once David's lineage went off, Esau broke free of our rule and began to conquer. “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing,” and said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” What did Cain do to Abel? He slew him. Nothing new under the sun: the same people doing the same exact thing. Rebekah told Jacob, “thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee”: how evil, to find comfort in killing your own brother.

Wisdom tells what became of Cain: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” The unrighteous is Cain. When he killed Abel it was not a tap on the back of the head; he brutally killed him in his fury. And Cain was killed too, the same violent way he killed Abel.

That is why Rebekah said, “why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” She knew: if Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau. You kill your brother, and you are going to die too.

precepts.label: Genesis 31:38-41
precepts.why:
Rebekah told Jacob to flee to her brother Laban's house because Esau wanted him dead, so he ran to Laban, and “Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.” He took rods of green poplar, hazel and chesnut, “pilled white strakes in them,” and set them before the flocks at the watering troughs. The stronger cattle conceived among the rods, “so the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.” “And the man increased exceedingly.”

So Jacob was Laban's shepherd; he took care of the sheep and the cattle. He was a shepherd just as Abel was a shepherd, and Esau was the man of the field just as Cain was a man of the field. The same two lines keep repeating.

And Jacob tells what that shepherding cost him: “This twenty years have I been with thee;” “That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it.” “Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.” “I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.”

Laban was a grimy man. He did Jacob dirty: Jacob took care of his cattle day and night, bore the losses himself, and Laban kept lowering his pay. Yet God increased Jacob exceedingly in spite of it.

thread.text: And yet for all that, when they be in the land of their enemies, I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, and to break my covenant with them: for I am the Lord their God.

precepts.label: Luke 1:68-74
precepts.why:
Leviticus 26 says that even “when they be in the land of their enemies”, like today here in America, “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”. Then: “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors. Luke 1 is saying the same thing in the New Testament.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ. He is the king, out of the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is what Leviticus 26 is saying: in the land of their enemies he will not cast them away.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”. That is the covenant of the ancestors in Leviticus 26:45, remembered for their sakes and brought to pass through Christ.

And what is it for? “that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. The God who brought our fathers out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen has not broken his covenant with us. He will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies so that we serve him without fear.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 22:9
thread.text: Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.

classes.title: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.label: Sirach 26:19-21
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.” Reading that, we might think only of agriculture or farming, but it is talking about much more than that, and Sirach 26 shows what.

“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” The strangers are the heathen, the other nations. Then it explains how you give your strength to them: “When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed.” A fruitful possession means you have a position, you have money, you are rich. Sow it with your own seed means sow it with your own people. You got money? Don't be going and marrying no damn white woman. What a lot of brothers do today, the first thing when they get money, is go marry a heathen. When you marry the heathen when you are rich, you are giving your strength unto strangers.

Instead, deal with your own people: start a family with the woman God created for you, “trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Your stock is your nationality, your race, your people. You are a son of God; why would you want to go deal with other nations?

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” When you marry your sisters and bring forth children among your people, your children and your race are magnified. Good descent means your children are not confused about what their nationality is, because you did not sow your seed among all different kinds of heathen women, as our forefathers did in the book of Nehemiah.

That is the law of Deuteronomy 22:9. When we go and deal with other nations, the fruit of the vineyard is defiled: the children brought forth, the descendants, are defiled and confused.

precepts.label: Romans 8:16
precepts.why:
“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed”. I don't care what country you are in, what state, what continent: these curses are following us. That's why we're getting shot down in the streets and killed left and right; the Most High has to do something to wake us back up. We are a destroyed nation, and we haven't understood that yet.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”. The curses are the sign. That is how we know we are the Israelites: the Bible gives us the signs to look out for, in Deuteronomy 28:15-68 and in Genesis 49, and if our spirit resonates with those signs, we are going to realize that we are the Israelites.

That is Romans 8:16: “The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”. That we, the Israelites, are the children of God. Not the whole world. The spirit itself, the Bible, bears witness with our spirit that we are those children.

And “for a wonder”: we are supposed to be wondering what happened. We are the greatest people on earth; how did we get so low? It will be upon our seed for ever, upon our children until Christ's return. Brothers want to argue the trinity while our people are being killed, holding the name Israel and refusing everything that goes with it. The sign is on us, and the spirit bears witness with ours: we are Israel, and we have to come back to the Lord.

thread.text: And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.

classes.title: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.label: John 3:3
precepts.why:
A lot of us are not finding comfort in the scriptures because we lack faith. You don’t believe the Bible can transform you. You don’t believe it can turn you into another man, that you could become a whole different person. But 1 Samuel 10:6 says it: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

John 3:3 says the same thing to Nicodemus: “Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Being turned into another man is being born again. The brother who drank a whole fifth in one night, the one who says, I can’t put it down, it’s a part of me, is not stuck being that man. Except he be born again, turned into another man, he cannot see the kingdom. The bottle is the battle, and the Bible is how you are turned into another man and win it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:34
precepts.why:
1 Samuel 10:6 says you “shalt be turned into another man.” 2 Esdras 14:34 tells you what your part is in that turning.

“Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart. We have to be transformed in the renewing of our minds. Transformed.

That is what the brother with the addiction runs from. He comes to the table having drunk a whole fifth in one night and says he is not an alcoholic. Even the white man knows the first step of recovery is to admit it: you have to realize you need help, that you are sick. Has he watched the classes on alcohol the Bishops and Deacons go over all the time? No. Why not? Because he is running away from his issues, and you cannot run away from that thing. You have to subdue your own understanding, reform your heart, and let the word turn you into another man, and then you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.

precepts.label: Isaiah 58:9
precepts.why:
Samuel asked Saul, “Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the Lord?” King Saul had an issue with being obedient to the Lord, and God called that disobedience evil in his sight. Saul answered, “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord”, and then, “But the people took of the spoil.” Was that a sign of godly sorrow? No, there was none involved. Isaiah 58:9 names what Saul was doing.

“Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity.”

What is the putting forth of the finger? That is blaming. Saul blamed the people right after saying he had kept Agag alive. He blamed the people for keeping the sheep and the best of the flocks, but did not take accountability for keeping Agag the Amalekite alive. So what does the Lord say? He is not going to hear any of us until we stop playing the blame game. The Lord answers, “Here I am”, when the finger is taken away.

Stop blaming others. How are you dealing with that situation? I am bitter against this person because they did this to me; I have hatred towards this person because of this. The Lord does not care about your reasoning or your justification, because every one of us will be judged according to our ways. The Lord sees how that person is treating you, and the same way he sees how you are reacting to that treatment. If you trust in the Lord, you act according to how God commanded you to deal with that situation, and then let the Lord deal with that person.

That is a building block of bitterness. Disobedience, then justifying yourself, then blaming others: the bitterness is compounded on sins that were already there. As 1 Samuel 15:22 says, “to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.”

classes.title: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.label: Ezekiel 8:14
precepts.why:
Manasseh “caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom”. That valley, Gehenna, was where Israel burned its garbage, our refuse; the Muslims call it Gehenna, their hell. Where garbage used to be burned, they burned their children, in honor of Baal.

There was an order to it. In the spring they held orgies in honor of Ashtoreth, the fertility goddess, a black Hamite deity whose star is Venus and whose nose is knocked off the statues. Everyone slept with everyone, and the women got pregnant. Nine months later, in the winter, came the bull god, Baal, the sun god the Egyptians called Apis. The babies were laid on the plates of the brass bull with a fire under it and around it; as they burned they wiggled off into the flame, and drums were beaten to drown out their screams. That is what Manasseh was doing, by the thousands. Carnival babies, Freaknik and the club today are the same worship of that goddess.

Why sacrifice the babies? Ashtoreth gave birth to a baby god, Tammuz, and Tammuz died as an infant. The same way she lost her child, the women had to lose theirs, and the same way she wept for her child, they had to weep for the children they sacrificed on the altar. That is why Jesus is always pictured as a baby with Mary.

Ezekiel saw it: “Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.” That is what they had to do once they were in that idolatry: weep for the babies they themselves had sacrificed. And it was worse than what is brought out here.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 12:3-7
precepts.why:
“So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.” Worse than the nations we were killing out of the land for doing the exact same thing. What does that mean? Wisdom of Solomon gives an idea.

“For it was thy will to destroy by the hands of our fathers both those old inhabitants of thy holy land”. Our fathers were Joshua, Caleb and the elders who succeeded Moses; when we entered the promised land we had to war with the nations already there. The old inhabitants were the Canaanites, the Hamites living in the land before we got there.

“Whom thou hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices”: odious works are filth, evil, vile things, and that is what Manasseh was doing. “And also those merciless murderers of children”: Manasseh did it and had the people do it. “and devourers of man’s flesh, and the feasts of blood”: cannibalism, drinking blood, eating flesh. Who knows what Manasseh was doing, but he was worse than the heathen, so we have to factor this in. “and the parents, that killed with their own hands souls destitute of help”: we were killing our own kids.

“That the land, which thou esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy colony of God’s children.” The Lord had us go in and kill those nations out of the land because they were doing these things. Then we got the land, turned around, and did the exact same thing and worse under Manasseh, as Ahab did in his time. Manasseh was one of the worst kings Judah ever had.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 21:16
precepts.why:
Kings tells the same account in its own way. It had already said Manasseh “hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols.” He went above the Amorites; Manasseh was a monster. Chronicles gives more of the detail: he “caused his children to pass through the fire”, ancient abortions, burning his babies alive; he observed times, used enchantments and witchcraft, dealt with a familiar spirit and with wizards; he was a sorcerer. And he put an idol in the temple.

Then Kings adds what Chronicles leaves out: “Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another.” Babies on babies. That is a lot of blood, from one end of Jerusalem to the other. And it was not only him: the people did the same thing, for this was “beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

Manasseh was behind a lot of death, sorcery and witchcraft; he did evil way beyond worthy of death. He killed babies, he went into witchcraft, he defiled the temple. And yet, when he was in affliction and humbled himself greatly, the Lord forgave Manasseh, heard his supplication, and put him back on the throne. The Lord has mercy on whom he will have mercy.

That is why it is so important for us to learn humility. People fall, and the Most High is able to raise them up again, like David. But don't abuse it. All of us in here ain't David; don't think, I can do what David did. No, negro, you ain't David. You're not Manasseh. You ain't Moses. The Lord puts it there to remind us that the graces and mercies of Christ were around back then too, from time to time. Don't get stupid and get prideful. Humility.

thread.text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.

classes.title: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.label: Psalms 10:17
precepts.why:
“For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” What is the heart? The mind. Ezra had prepared his mind to seek the Lord his God. We are in captivity, always working and tired; some days you get stressed. But the Most High has to remind us that we are living in the last days. So brothers, prepare your minds; sisters, prepare your minds.

David shows who the Lord prepares: “Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear”. We are the humble. We are supposed to humble ourselves to whatever the Bible says we ought to do.

And when we humble ourselves, the Lord hears our desire and prepares our hearts. We will prepare our minds. That is what Ezra did before he went to teach Israel, and that is what is required of us now, as we watch Iran and Israel go to war and America get involved, and more of our people wake up and repent.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:17
precepts.why:
Why prepare our minds and our spirits? Because war is imminent. We are seeing Iran and Israel at war and America getting involved, and the wars are only going to get worse. What we see right now is a birthing pain. Yet all of us are supposed to rejoice, because the scriptures already told us this was going to happen.

Sirach says: “They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight”. All of us that fear the Lord will prepare our minds, so that whatever evil comes upon the earth, we will remain faithful in serving the Lord.

That is Ezra's example: a heart prepared, and a soul humbled in the Lord's sight, ready to seek the law, do it, and teach it, whatever comes.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:3-4
precepts.why:
Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law and to teach it. Sirach shows why: “A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him, as an oracle.” We must trust in the laws of God, and the law will be faithful unto us.

“Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard”. We have to prepare what to say. Prepare what to say in prayer when we speak to the Most High, and we will be heard. Prepare what to say and teach in the streets, and we will be heard. We must prepare to lead, guide and organize blacks and Hispanics.

“and bind up instruction, and then make answer.” Bind up the instruction first, and then make answer. That is how Ezra could teach in Israel statutes and judgments: he had prepared his heart before he opened his mouth.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:17
precepts.why:
This is to the brothers who teach, the up-and-coming soldiers in the MOV program. Ezra prepared his heart to teach in Israel, and the Lord says: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

Who is speaking? The Most High said, I have made thee a watchman. It is not the Bishop that made you a watchman. It is not the deacons, and it is not the captains. The Lord called you to be a watchman. That is why you were called into this truth: to warn our people, to warn Israel that they need to repent.

Habakkuk shows the watchman's posture: “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. He is awake and paying attention. As watchmen we must be faithful and pay attention to the signs of the times, hear the word at the Lord's mouth, and give Israel warning from him.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:32
precepts.why:
“He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise. He taketh the wise in their own craftiness”. The crafty are the nations, in particular Esau, that counsel against us and keep exploiting, oppressing and colonizing with imperialism. It is the same as Psalms 21: “they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.” Their counsel is carried headlong; they are going to fall headlong and bust their forehead. “They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.”

“But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.” From Esau's sword, the nations' sword. Who is the poor? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

Write it down, brothers: when the scripture talks about the poor, it is talking about Israel, the poor of his people who trust in Zion. That was an easy one, and every soldier should know it.

And before the Lord saves the poor from the sword, the wicked has to be identified. The man of sin must be revealed, so that the whole earth knows who he is: the nation that bombed country after country, removed leader after leader, and made the earth to tremble.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:21
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them.” That sounds just like Malachi 4: “the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”, and “it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Nuclear fire is coming to America. And David goes on: “Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.” Neither root nor branch: their children will be cut off too.

Isaiah shows why the children are cut off: “Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers.” For the sins of their forefathers. The forefathers committed the crime, got the bag from us, took the wealth, took everything from us, and now the children are left holding the bag. Esau, and not just Esau: Elam, Ishmael, the Hamites. All of them got wealthy off the backs of the Israelites; all of them had us in slavery one way or another.

It is done “that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities. For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew.” Son and nephew goes right back to Psalm 21 and the end of Malachi 4: their seed destroyed from among the children of men.

Why? “For they intended evil against thee: they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.” They imagine evil devices and evil counsels against us, but “He disappointeth the devices of the crafty”, and “he saveth the poor from the sword.” The poor are Israel: “the poor of his people shall trust in it.” So the fiery oven is for the nations that enslaved us, down to their children, and the Lord saves his poor from their sword.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:17
precepts.why:
David says it plainly: “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” A sacrifice for the Lord is not so much an animal. What he wants laid on the altar is a broken spirit, a broken and contrite heart, which is a broken mind.

That is the same thing Psalms 34:18 says: “The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart.” Man by nature is arrogant; we do what we want to do. So the Most High will put you in a position where he has to break you, break you down and shame you, bring you down to the lowest, until you realize: I can't do these things no more, I have to humble myself and do better, for the Lord's sake first and foremost, for my own sake, and for my people's sake as an example.

Isaiah shows where the Lord dwells when he comes near. “the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity” is the Father, and eternity is his domain, the upper room, the top floor. Yet he says, “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.” The Father and his Son deal with and dwell with the humble in spirit.

That broken spirit is the sacrifice worthy of his time. Being haughty and arrogant and offering the best sacrifices is a complete waste of time, because humility comes before honor. That is how Manasseh, a man the law said should die, found mercy: he humbled himself, and God would not despise that broken heart.

thread.text: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

classes.title: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:22
precepts.why:
Psalms 51:16: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” David is saying, you don’t desire sacrifice, otherwise I would give it to you; you don’t care about that either. The Lord revealed to David, I don’t care about sacrifices. And Saul didn’t listen either.

“And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” Samuel is asking the question: does the Lord require sacrifices above obeying what he tells you to do?

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” To hearken is to listen and humble yourself. That is better than the fat of rams.

So “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” The sacrifice God accepts is a broken spirit. The animals were just temporary; your mind being broken and humbled is the best sacrifice the Lord desires. You can offer and sacrifice all you want, but make sure you offer with a good heart. “Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt offering and whole burnt offering: then shall they offer bullocks upon thine altar.” Once the sacrifices of righteousness are offered, then the bullocks on the altar become acceptable.

precepts.label: Sirach 35:17
precepts.why:
Psalms 51:17 says “a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” Ecclesiasticus 35:17 shows what happens when the humbled one prays.

“The prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds.” It pierces the clouds: the Lord hears it. “And till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.”

That is David in Psalms 51. When Nathan confronted him after Bathsheba and Uriah, he did not stay the smartest guy in the room. He said, you are right, I am guilty: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.” He kept the promise he made in Psalms 32:5, “I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid.” He held himself accountable, and you have to hold yourself accountable when it comes to your sins.

The bones that were broken were his humbling: being confronted with his wrong, confessing it and acknowledging it, and the consequences that followed. And out of that broken, humbled place he prayed, “Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.” That is the prayer of the humble, the one that pierces the clouds, and it is the same humility that brought mercy to King Manasseh.

thread.label: Psalms 51:17
thread.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Psalms 51:11
precepts.why:
Solomon was knocked down, and David, the man after the Lord's own heart, was knocked down. Did they stay down? No. We are not in the business of staying down; we get knocked down and keep going. Satan tells us to stay down, and some brothers and sisters want you to stay down, but that is not what God said. “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” That is what God is looking for.

So what do we pray when Satan knocks us down? David prayed it: “Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” We pray that the Lord does not remove his Holy Spirit from us, because that is what keeps us standing.

“Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.” You have to look at the truth with a joyful and glad heart, because you cannot live without it; it is part of your system, your life. Where else can you go? We do not give up our position; we pray that the Lord keeps strengthening us.

“Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” When we get back up, our job is to teach, because we have been through the trial and tribulation and understand what it takes. We go right back to the business we left off, teaching our people their transgressions so they do not fall into what we fell into. Do we give that up to go sit on the couch, or sit in the back and puff up on evil?

Nobody sees the prayer, the crying at night, the tears when you are home alone thinking, I could have done better. That is the broken and contrite heart God will not despise. Tell Satan to bring it on. With a position or without it, be the same: a trooper. And when a brother is knocked down, do not applaud it; fast and pray for him, because he is still fighting the same battle you are, and your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his.

thread.label: Psalms 55:22
thread.text: Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.

classes.title: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.label: Matthew 11:28
precepts.why:
The bottle says, forget your pain; the Bible says, “Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.” The bottle says, numb your sorrow. Christ answers that lie: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”

The bottle offers to carry your burden for you. It talks to you like scripture in a dark room with one light over the table: drink me, I can take away thy sorrows; you're depressed, don't worry about it; you're stressed out, put the kids to bed early and drink me. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

Christ is the one who actually takes the weight. The labouring and heavy laden are told to come to him, not to the liquor store, and he gives rest. The bottle only numbs the sorrow until tomorrow; casting the burden on the Lord is how he sustains you and keeps the righteous from being moved.

precepts.label: Romans 8:1
precepts.why:
The bottle says, you are a failure. You ain't nothing. You're going to be the same person you always were. The Bible says: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

Guess what? You can repent. The bottle says you're a failure; the Bible says you can repent and become a new man.

But it starts with acknowledging it: I'm an alcoholic. I'm a fornicator, an adulterer, a liar, a thief; I deal with envy, covetousness, idolatry. That is where the change happens. And acknowledging it is not enough; you have to work on fixing those things. You can't say, I'm an alcoholic, and keep going out drinking.

No condemnation belongs to those who walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh. The man chained to the bottle is walking after the flesh; the man who casts his burden on the Lord and walks in the Spirit is free of the condemnation the bottle keeps whispering over him.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7
precepts.why:
The bottle says, you can't change. You're the same; you're going to be that same person. The Bible says, “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.”

The law of the Lord converts the soul: it changes a man. So the lie that you can't change is answered by the perfect law of God. You can repent and become a new man.

That is the other side of casting your burden on the Lord. You don't just hand him the weight; you take on his law, and his law turns you into somebody different. The bottle keeps you drunk and stupid, the way the enemy wants it, with a liquor store in every black neighborhood and weed stores everywhere to keep you high, drunk and stupid. The law of the Lord makes the simple wise and converts the soul out of that.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:18
precepts.why:
The bottle says, take another drink. You can handle it; drink some more. The Bible says, “And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.”

The bottle wants to fill you: drink me and be filled with my love. It says, you're alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. I love you more than water. You don't need to eat today; I'll make the food taste better. You can't sleep; I can put you to sleep so fast you won't even realize it. The bottle starts talking like scripture: I am that I am, the comfort of them all.

That is excess, and it destroys the body too. Alcohol builds fat around your organs and your belly, raises your risk of heart disease, high blood pressure and type two diabetes, makes you hungrier and drives you to fast food. Four or five shots a drink every day is thousands of calories a week, and then you wonder why you can't lose weight or climb a flight of stairs.

The command is to be filled with something else: the Spirit. Cast your burden on the Lord and be filled with his Spirit, not with the bottle.

precepts.label: Psalms 74:18
precepts.why:
The psalm ends its first cry with, “O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?” How does the enemy blaspheme? By making our signs their signs. White Jesus is blasphemy. White angels are blasphemy. All these whitewashed images are blasphemy; it is evil.

Further down Asaph says it again: “Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Lord, and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.” The foolish people are the nations, primarily, and in some instances our own people too.

To blaspheme is to speak evil of his name, his reputation. White Jesus is blasphemy. He died for all people, the gospel is for all people, all nations can be saved: blasphemy. He isn't the son of God, he doesn't exist, I'm an atheist, evolution: blasphemy. His name is blasphemed every day all around the world.

That is why the enemy is not only the one who burned the sanctuary and the synagogues, as Babylon and Assyria did. The enemy is also the one who keeps reproaching God's name by painting over his people, so that “We see not our signs.” We don't see statues of David or Solomon or Christ as black men; we see their images, their depictions.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:48
precepts.why:
The psalm says of the enemy, “they set up their ensigns for signs.” What are their ensigns for signs? Cesare Borgia; Mother Mary, white Mary; baby white Jesus; white prophets; the Last Supper; the Sistine Chapel. Posing themselves as God, as the prophets, as the angels, as the heavenly Father: whitewashing our ensigns and making our ensigns their signs.

Maccabees shows it was done before: they “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The book of the law is our Bible, and the heathen sought to paint the likeness of their own images into it.

They made our signs their signs. The Greeks did it, the Romans did it, Spain did it, Portugal did it, Britain did it, the Dutch, the French: they all did it, and they still do it. It was blasphemy back then, and it is blasphemy now.

That is why Asaph cries, “We see not our signs.” The heathen painted themselves into the book of the law, and our people no longer see their own images in the scriptures that were written about them.

classes.title: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis
Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.label: Matthew 4:17
precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. You cannot have a good understanding if you are not keeping the commandments. It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while you are not observing the laws of God. There is no way around it. All the foolishness that gets exposed comes from those that refuse to repent and keep God's commandments.

That is why Christ's message from the start was this: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

So many of our brothers and sisters out in the world have yet to come to grips with what we are here for. Being an Israelite in Christ is not about dressing up as an Israelite. It's not about arguing with white folks in the streets. It's not about flexing your muscles and trying to be a tough guy. And no, it is not about multiple wives.

Being an Israelite in Christ is about observing the Most High God's commandments and faith in his Son, so that we don't die when the Lord returns. The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and you are at risk if you do not repent and seek the kingdom. Point blank, period.

Those who deny Christ and deny keeping the commandments, because they want to fulfil their own lust, come up with absurd breakdowns of scripture. Without repentance there is no good understanding.

thread.label: Psalms 124:1
thread.text: If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, now may Israel say;

classes.title: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.label: Lamentations 3:22
precepts.why:
King David says, “If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, now may Israel say”: the Lord was on Israel’s side, “when men rose up against us”, when the nations rose up against us. Think about that. The only reason we are still breathing is the mercy of the Lord.

Lamentations says it plainly: “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” That we, brothers and sisters, are still here is only because of the Lord. With the weapons Esau has and the weapons the nations have, if the Lord put the spirit on them to do what they do and gave them free reign with us, we would all have been wiped out.

Read on: “They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” “The Lord is my portion, saith my soul”. His compassion does not fail, and that is why Psalms 124 can say the nations did not swallow us up.

precepts.label: Numbers 14:18
precepts.why:
“The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression”. Being longsuffering is one of the characteristics we must take on with our brothers and our sisters. A lot of times we are carnal and have no patience with each other. A brother offends you, or does what you think is an offence that he may not even see as one, and you get all in your feelings; sisters get in their feelings about something somebody said or the way somebody moves toward them. We are all different spirits joining together for one common goal. We are not all going to get along, but we all have to be longsuffering with each other and endure it.

Then: “and by no means clearing the guilty”. Why is he of great mercy but will by no means clear the guilty? Just because you sin and are not judged immediately does not mean you will not be judged; you are still guilty of that sin. And to get that great mercy, you have to repent and forsake your sins. The ones he will not clear are those that do not repent, and he visits “the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation.”

So back to Psalms 124: it is of the Lord’s mercy, longsuffering with Israel, that the men who rose up against us did not swallow us up.

precepts.label: Isaiah 17:12
precepts.why:
Psalms 124 goes on: “Then they had swallowed us up quick”, the nations would have swallowed us up, “Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul:” “Then the proud waters had gone over our soul.” The waters are not the water of affliction. Write it down, brothers: the waters in Psalms 124 are the nations.

Isaiah proves it: “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” Keep reading: “The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters”. He is comparing the nations to waters.

“but God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.” That is the Lord being on our side: the proud waters, the nations, rush against Israel, and God rebukes them.

precepts.label: Revelation 17:15
precepts.why:
One more precept on the waters: “The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” The waters are peoples and nations again, and the one sitting on them is America. Look at where America sits: bases and fleets all over the earth.

So what could Russia do with this? America does not have to send its entire fleet to Russia or to China; it is already there, it does not have to go anywhere. If I was Trump, I might boast too. Look at the weaponry he has.

That is the power of the nations the Psalm is talking about. “Then the proud waters had gone over our soul”, but “Blessed be the Lord, who hath not given us as a prey to their teeth.” Because of the Lord’s mercies, “Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers: the snare is broken, and we are escaped.” And “Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth”: that name is God’s commandments with faith in his Son.

thread.label: Psalms 140:1-4
thread.text: Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;

classes.title: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.label: Malachi 1:1-4
precepts.why:
The evil man and the violent man of Psalms 140 has a name, and Malachi gives it. “I have loved you, saith the Lord.” Israel asks, “Wherein hast thou loved us?” And the answer: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” He loved Jacob just like he loved Abel, and he hated Esau. Laying his mountains and his heritage waste means God allowed him to be overthrown.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: we lost all, we are going back to being vagabonds. “but we will return and build the desolate places”: build themselves back up as an empire, just like Cain built that city. And the Lord answers, “They shall build, but I will throw down.”

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: the beginning and the end of wickedness. “and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: no repentance, no salvation, no kingdom, ever. Not even the good ones, so some of you coons out there.

So when David prays “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man” and “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”, this is who he is praying against: Esau, Edom, the people the Lord hated and against whom he hath indignation for ever.

precepts.label: Matthew 11:12
precepts.why:
“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom of heaven, that's Israel, and Israel suffereth violence. The violent that take it by force are the Romans, and Esau is the Romans.

That puts a name on the man of Psalms 140. The Bible calls the evil man, the violent man, the wicked, and Esau is the violent man, the wicked man. “They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips”: they are liars. And they “have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

So David's cry, “preserve me from the violent man”, is Israel's cry to be kept from the hands of Esau, the Romans, who have done violence to the kingdom of heaven from the days of John the Baptist until now.

precepts.label: Daniel 4:17
precepts.why:
“The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” The king in this nation right now, in 2026, is Donald Trump. His heart is in the hand of the Lord, and whatever way the Lord wants him to go, he is going to go, and he is going to fulfill what the Lord has in store.

Daniel shows why: “This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men.” God rules in the kingdoms of men. God is the ultimate ruler.

And what does he do? He “giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.” He gives the kingdom over to whomever he chooses, and he sets over it the basest of men: the least of men, the bottom feeders. The bottom feeders are ruling us right now. Biden, Trump, Putin, all of them: they are the bottom.

So the king’s heart turning like rivers of water and the Most High setting up the basest of men are the same truth. Trump is not ruling by his own power. He is set up by the Most High and turned whithersoever he will, a sword in the hand of God to bring judgment on the nations.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:15
precepts.why:
Solomon says it again in chapter 3: “That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.”

It is the same as “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. One generation comes and another goes; the old die and the young are born. The sun has its cycle, the wind has its circuits, and the rivers run into the sea and return again. Generations have their circuits and cycles the same way.

So what is to be has already been. Before our generation it was already in the past, only “There is no remembrance of former things”. That is why a man can stand in a moment and feel, I remember this.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 6:10
precepts.why:
What is the thing that hath been? Solomon names it: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man”. So he explains it himself: the thing that have been is man.

Just like the wind, the sun, the moon and the rivers have a flow, likewise man: we come and we go. You and I have been here before, in different cycles of life. That is why it is called deja vu, a French term that literally means already seen: the sensation of having already experienced a situation even though you know it is happening for the first time.

Already seen, because you are already meant to be there. The prophets saw things that came to pass. When the prophets saw us going on slave ships, we had to live out what they saw. So when John saw America in flames, we have to live out what John already saw. We are catching up to the prophecies, and what leads up to them is already set in motion. You can't change it.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 8:1
precepts.why:
“Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing?” The wise man knows the interpretation of the thing. And “a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine”.

The thing that hath been, in Ecclesiastes 1, is talking about man. Man has been around before, but “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.” It takes wisdom to interpret that thing.

So the wise man understands the cycle: the generations pass and come again, and what the prophets already saw is what we are living out now. The wise man knows it is man that hath been, and that is why there is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
“behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power”. That's us. Our oppressors have power: they organize themselves, pass laws and policies, colonize, oppress and exploit. And the Israelites had no comforter.

So what is supposed to comfort us? Paul says: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Whatsoever was written aforetime means this Bible, and it was written for our learning. We ought to learn from what happened to the Israelites, to the apostles, and to Christ.

“comfort of the scriptures”: this is our comforter. The scriptures of this Bible are where the oppressed find comfort, and that is what we need to hope in.

The oppressors hold all the cards right now, and the one who has no comforter in the world has one in the word. If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, the nations would have swallowed us up; it is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed.

precepts.label: Job 3:11
precepts.why:
Because of verse 1, with no comforter and all the power on the side of our oppressors, Solomon says: “Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.” Better than both is he “which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.” He would rather praise the dead, who are not going through the oppression, than the living, who are depressed, oppressed, suppressed, pressed all kinds of ways.

Job said the same: “Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Job was going through tribulation hell: his wife on him, his kids dying, the skin disease, his lands, everything lost. Why didn't I just die already? Why am I still here?

“For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest”. If he had slept, meaning been dead, he would have been at rest, not going through the hell he was going through; or as “infants which never saw light”, meaning stillborn. “There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest. There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.” We are the prisoners. In death they don't have to deal with oppressors no more.

That is how heavy the oppression of Ecclesiastes 4:1 is. And the only reason we are still breathing is the mercy of the Lord, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth.

thread.label: Isaiah 9:6-7
thread.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: John 14:8-9
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the son that is given “The everlasting Father.” Most Christians, and even some Israelites, cannot explain that, because they have not figured out that the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They say we always spoke to the Father. No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That is why he is called the everlasting Father. John 14 is a precept for it.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” See Christ’s response: “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father. But what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I am your Father, your everlasting Father. You were brought forth through me.

Remember, Christ is the only begotten of the Father. That means the Father created only Christ, and then told Christ to create everything else. So when Isaiah names the child born unto us “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”, it is because everything that exists was brought forth through him. That is why Philip, who had been with him so long, should have known him.

precepts.label: John 1:1-3
precepts.why:
In case anyone is still confused about why Christ is called “The everlasting Father”, John 1 settles it. We have to shake the Christian thoughts.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God.” God is a plural there.

Then the part that matters: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ was not any thing made that was made. The Father only begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created.

That is why he said to Philip, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” I created all of this. That is too heavy for a Negro, because you have Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning too, but the Most High has shown us. Let it marinate.

So the child born and the son given in Isaiah 9:6, with the government upon his shoulder, is the same one who made all things: the Word, the mighty God, the everlasting Father.

precepts.label: Matthew 13:31-32
precepts.why:
“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Christ explains that increase in Matthew 13: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.” If you grew up in the city you may not know what a mustard seed looks like; it is one of the smallest of all seeds.

“but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown: that is the increase of his government. It starts small. What we have here is small. We may think we have a lot, but this is nothing yet; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

And the kingdom of heaven is a government, not a church group. That is why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, commandments and statutes: to set up a government you need everything that makes a community, and God’s laws are going to filter everything for us. Right now we think small. God says think bigger. A house? Bigger. Property? Bigger. The world is ours, and for the world to be ours we have to be able to set all of that up.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Everything you lay your eyes on, every object and invention, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt, but that is not what God made. Untapped greatness is waiting to bud; remove the doubt and the fear and let the Lord work on that head.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:12-21
precepts.why:
The mustard seed government is small now, and we think small. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” Solomon learned wisdom and gave it out freely, and that is what we are doing today: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God. “For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom we become the friends of God. And it comes from learning, not once but daily; that is what the classes every day are about.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.” You might say you know how the world was made. You don’t: what elements make the air, what elements were made for the sun? Solomon understood that. He knew “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. He knew “the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons”, “The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.”

“The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts cameras on animals, even in their butts, to learn how they defecate, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. Solomon knew “the furies of wild beasts”, “the violence of winds”, the tornadoes and storms, “the reasonings of men”, “the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”, which herb is for what, and “all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We are not even on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when he does we will be on that level and greater. That is what the mustard seed is about: we start small and it grows. This is the beginning of that government.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:5-6
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the government shall be upon his shoulder, “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice.” Jeremiah says the same: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.” That righteous Branch is Christ.

“and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. Some of us in here may not want that either: I don’t want no justice and judgment, hell no. Yes, it is coming anyway.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

So the throne of David in Isaiah 9 is the reign of this King, the Branch raised unto David. The increase of his government is a kingdom of judgment and justice, of law and order, and in his days Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. That is why we learn God’s laws now: it is the government we are going to live under.

precepts.label: Isaiah 58:1
precepts.why:
“The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see. Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand.” The high mountain is the government, America. The banner we lift up upon it is the Bible. So in the midst of all this chaos, Isaiah sees the prophets still going out teaching.

“Exalt the voice unto them”: that is what we do, and Isaiah 58 says how. “Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins.” We exalt the voice, we spare not, we lift up our voice as a trumpet.

“Shake the hand”: warn our people, “that they may go into the gates of the nobles.” The nations have drunk Babylon's wine, her lies and philosophies, what Daniel calls her policy, and therefore the nations are mad. War is coming, and in the midst of all that war, the prophets are still crying aloud, showing our people their transgression so they can be saved.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:11
precepts.why:
Isaiah sees the war coming on Babylon and the prophets still lifting up the banner and exalting the voice. Paul says why we do it: “Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men.” In Job he is called the king of terrors. We know what the Lord is going to do. The Lord set us up as watchmen, and since we know the terror of the Lord, we must persuade men.

“But we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.”

Who are we trying to persuade? Our people, in the midst of all kinds of sin. So brothers, we must be studying, so that when we come across our people we are able to help them. The scripture says the whole head is sick: we are sick individuals ourselves. But we must learn to discipline ourselves, and we must learn how to persuade our people to change their lives.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 1:9-10
precepts.why:
These are the kind of people we are trying to persuade to change: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane.” It is for our people who are lawless.

“For murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers.” If you knew a brother murdered his father or his mother, you would not treat him the same; your instant reaction is, bro, you cold, who does that? “For manslayers”: imagine being cool with a brother and not knowing the whole time he had bodies on him. But there is repentance for those spirits. These are the spirits we are trying to win over and get to submit to the Lord.

“For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”: women with all kinds of men, men with all kinds of women, and homosexuality. There is repentance for all of these sins. Some of us are struggling with one, two, three, four, five of these. God damn. We have demons on us.

The only way to get it out is to have one counsellor of a thousand and open up. That is the problem: some of you don't want to open up, and by the time we find out what you are struggling with, it's too late to help. It doesn't mean you can't repent, but it is a lot harder because you kept it secret so long, and by the time you tell us you are already having sex and we have to throw you out. Repent, submit yourself to the Lord, and stay close with the pack.

“For menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.” How many of us lie? We all lie. Why didn't you come to the Sabbath? My back, I was tired: a lie. Why didn't you come to the new moon? I got off work late: a lie, because in your mind you already said, I'll go next time.

Can you persuade a murderer, a lesbian, a homosexual to change their life? Can you turn a liar or a thief into a soldier? You can, and the proof is that you are sitting in the building. Don't say only Deacon Eythan or Black Rhino knows how to talk to people.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:63-64
precepts.why:
We are to persuade our people, but this is what we have to overcome: “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.” That is what we do. We sin, and we hide our sin.

The Lord says, I know your inventions. I know why you watch HBO at night; I know why you like Spartacus, why you like Power. I know you love to smoke weed and spray yourself with cologne right before you come to the Sabbath, and then security says, that brother smells like weed. Keep smoking weed and you will end up face down in the street like the man in the video, calling the officer papi.

Some brothers are tied to unbelieving wives who cook pork on the same grill next to your lawful food, still go to the club and don't respect you, and you refuse to leave. Sisters are tied to unbelieving men. There is no love among our people, and we are caught up in these sins, lawless, like 1 Timothy 1:9.

You can hide it from the brothers and the sisters, but you cannot hide it from the Lord. He knows your inventions and what you think in your heart. So before we can persuade our people, we have to get ourselves right.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:61
precepts.why:
“That there should not be such heaviness in their destruction, as shall be joy over them that are persuaded to salvation.” We must persuade men to salvation. We see the wars going on with Iran; we see the prophecies coming to pass and escalating. But the Lord told us, go persuade my people to salvation, go bring them into the sanctuary.

How do we do it? Proverbs 25:15: “By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.” To forbear is to patiently restrain. A prince is a very high rank, and with long patience you can persuade even princes. And what does Israel mean? Prince of the power. We have to be patient with the Israelites.

As teachers, be patient and strategic. When you are having that conversation, don't think they are just wicked as hell; they might actually repent, but you were not patient enough. Be diplomatic, learn how to reason. When people come up to you in the street, don't hit them with the first death scripture. You were once in that spot, and the only reason we are in this building is that the Lord opened our eyes.

A soft tongue breaks the bone: somebody can be pissed with you, and you respond with peace. You from Brooklyn, from DC, from PG County, want to respond even more aggressive. But the joy over one of our people persuaded to salvation is greater than the heaviness over the destruction of the rest.

thread.text: For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north:

precepts.label: Jeremiah 16:14
precepts.why:
“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God.” That is America going into space; America was the first there, and America invented the airplane that ascends “above the heights of the clouds.” “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north.” That is the Monroe Doctrine, now the Donroe Doctrine. The congregation is Mexico, Central and South America, Panama, Puerto Rico, Dominica, Jamaica, Trinidad and the Caribbean islands, where the twelve tribes of Israel are. America, the king of Babylon, the oppressor, sits upon the congregation and rules over us: fall in line, or what we did to Maduro we will do to you. And it is in the sides of the north, North America; that is why its treaty with Europe is called the North Atlantic Treaty.

Jeremiah shows where Israel is: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north.” The land of the north is North America. It is going to be said that the Lord brought the children of Israel out of this side of the world.

“and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” Israel is in North America and all through this hemisphere, and 2 Esdras speaks of the ten tribes coming to this side of the world.

So the one who sits on the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north is sitting on Israel. According to prophecy, America will be sitting on these congregations in the last days, during the fourth seal, and bad things are about to happen on this side of the world. But the Lord will bring his people up out of the land of the north.
