precepts.label: Deuteronomy 6:25
precepts.why:
“Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” To know who the unrighteous are, you have to know what righteousness is, and the law defines it: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

That is what righteousness is: observing to do all the commandments before the Lord, as he commanded. So the unrighteous who will not inherit the kingdom are those who will not do the commandments.

That is the problem with Christianity. It is not that the Lord's arm is too short or his ear too heavy; it is that your sins have separated between you and your God. They are not trying to transform their lives to that of the nation of Israel according to the holy scriptures. And that is why Paul lists fornicators, idolaters, adulterers and the rest: every one of them breaks the commandments that are our righteousness.

precepts.label: Romans 10:1-4
precepts.why:
The Christian says, oh no, that's not the righteousness; go to Romans 10:4: “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.” See, we ain't got to keep no laws, so that cancels out Deuteronomy 6:25. No, numbskull. We don't run from scriptures; we explain and edify on the scriptures.

Christ is the end of the law of animal sacrifice for righteousness. Christ took the place of the animal sacrifice. And where they think they have you, “to every one that believeth”, read verse one for the context: “Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.”

The whole subject is Israel being saved. Israel had “a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge”, “going about to establish their own righteousness”. Christ is our righteousness in the law because he suffered and took the place of the law of sacrifice. That does not do away with the commandments of Deuteronomy 6:25; it is why the unrighteous, who will not keep them, still shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:28
precepts.why:
“Be not deceived: neither fornicators”, “nor adulterers”. Fornication covers the whole list of sexual sins in Leviticus 18. And for the porno brothers, Christ said: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.”

So porn falls into that category. It is adultery in the heart, and adulterers shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

Who still struggles with porn? Not who is always watching; who still struggles with it? Nine hands went up in the room. The fight is real, and it has to be named for what it is before it can be fought.

precepts.label: Romans 6:12-15
precepts.why:
“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” The word reign means to rule: don't let sin rule your mortal body. Every brother says, I got the porn under control, I am in control. There's no such thing as control of sin. Once you start obeying that lust, it has you in control; you don't have it in control.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.” Men and women are alive from the dead. We have to submit ourselves to Christ; he is our commander, our leader, and what he says we must do.

“For sin shall not have dominion over you”: Paul is reiterating. Dominion goes back to reign in verse 12. “for ye are not under the law”, the law of sacrifice, “but under grace”, the grace of Christ. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace?” Should we keep watching porn because we're not under the law of sacrifice? “God forbid.”

One brother said, I got it under control. In a store, thinking about porn, he was on his phone looking at it, forgot where he was, took his pecker out and started looking at all the ladies. Does that sound like he had it under control? He got arrested; he's in jail. Another decided to look at porn while he drove home, and bam, he crashed. It has you in check. You need a checklist in your mind so you can say, I'm messed up, I need help, because I could die or I could be in jail. That is sin reigning, and the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:76-78
precepts.why:
What happens when sin reigns in your body and has dominion over you? “And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” He is the guide of those who keep his commandments and precepts.

“let not your sins weigh you down”: sometimes you fall in the midst of sin, and Satan gets in your ear and whispers, you're no good, you need to leave this truth, the Lord can't use a person like you. Well, he used Samson. He used David. He used a lot of our forefathers that fell to sin. “and let not your iniquities lift up themselves”: don't let them rise back up in your body again.

“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through!” You may say, I'm not bound with my sin. Bound in your sins is sin reigning in your body and having dominion over you. Just like no man can travel through that path, we can't reach you with the scriptures any more. Your heart is hardened, your sin has dominated your life, and you're not you anymore. The scriptures have no effect on you.

“It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Death and destruction: that is the final outcome, brothers. Stop watching the porn. “And such were some of you: but ye are washed”: that is the way out, not staying bound.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:6
precepts.why:
At the sit-down with the men from theology school, this was read to them: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”. Who is the us? Read up in the chapter and it is talking about the nation of Israel. “and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

Christ holds the title of God, but do not confuse that with his Father. Christ is called the everlasting Father because he created us. God the Father begat Christ, which is the creation of God, and Christ created us. It was read to them plain and simple, taking time, and you could hear it: Christ is called the mighty God and the everlasting Father. They still could not get it. They said creation does not mean creation, it means something else.

That is what Paul feared: “as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.” The serpent was a real slick one. He tricked Eve, like he is tricking the people in these Christian churches, when the scriptures are so plain to be understood.

It is a simple thing that Christ had an earthly father named Joseph, through Joseph's seed. It is a simple thing that Christ is not the same person as his Father. Many scriptures were gone through showing that the Father and the Son are two different people, and the confusion comes from the Christian churches.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 31:1
precepts.why:
The theology school men came preaching the promise of Genesis 12, that in Abraham all the families of the earth are blessed, as if it meant every nation. But “At the same time, saith the Lord, will I be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.” All the families in Genesis chapter 12 are all the families of Israel.

That is why it is very important to go precept upon precept. There is no scripture that shows Christ came for all the families of the other nations. It is impossible.

Afterwards he was asked: name me one scripture where God named another nation by name that he is going to redeem or save in the last days. He said it ain't in there. So what are we talking about, then? God named Israel by name to be saved and redeemed, and no other nation in the New Testament.

So where are they getting it from? Theology is a dangerous drug. That is “another gospel, which ye have not accepted”, the gospel for all nations, and Paul says of those who receive it, “ye might well bear with him.”

precepts.label: Amos 3:1-2
precepts.why:
“Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”. You Israelites only. The Lord does not know any other family. That is plain to be understood, and it matches Jeremiah 31, the God of all the families of Israel.

One of them still said the scripture does not mean that, after it was read to him plain: out of all the families of the earth, you only have I known. When your ears are closed and your eyes are blinded, you will never hear it or see it.

These cemetery schools are dangerous for our community. The Lord showed our people that theology school has been lying and bamboozling our people to keep them lost, in despair, oppressed and under the hand of the white man. White supremacy taught them the Bible. They get a certificate from going to school and learning the curriculum, paper that can burn. We get a reward for keeping God's laws, statutes and commandments: an everlasting reward with the Father.

That is the simplicity that is in Christ, and the other Jesus and the other gospel from theology school corrupt it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:54-56
precepts.why:
This was read to finish it. “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” We all come from Adam. Who did God choose? He chose Israel.

“All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes”. The planet earth was made for the children of Israel. Who is the our? The Israelites. It was read plain and simple, and the man still said no, on camera, after he read it himself.

“As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle”. God said the other nations are nothing. Spittle is the little drool running down your cheek when the workout gets too hard. God made it plain.

We walked in there in sincerity and true faith, not told anything beforehand, and they tried to bamboozle us. But the Lord got the victory. If after all those scriptures they still believe Christ has no father, that Christ, God and the Holy Spirit are one person, and that the other nations are chosen, then “ye might well bear with him.” It is time for our people to wake up. He saved the Israelites for last, to come back and take this planet over in true righteousness.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 6:3
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves”. Every brother and sister must examine themselves, and nobody can prove you but you. Ask yourself what you are doing that keeps you from growing in the spirit of Christ, and what you need help with. Do not wait until you hit rock bottom. The faith is the scriptures, and you must constantly examine yourself to see that you are still in it, because Satan can bind us while we still think we are in the truth, hardly reading, hardly studying, hardly watching class.

Knowing yourself means knowing your triggers and your weak point. If you are covetous, you should not have a job dealing with money. If you are lustful, you should not be watching certain videos or listening to R&B heavy. Music, movies and social media will lead you to porn. My lust and your lust might be different, but if I know myself, I know mine. So when the thought comes you say, self, we ain't going to do that today, turn it off and meditate on the scriptures. If you do not examine yourself, you are reprobate, and you let Satan use your body to do whatever he wants.

Why does it matter so much? “Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed”. Satan wants us to shame the ministry, and he makes us believe it is just a little thing. But people want to prove us wrong. They are ready to pick at any little thing: see what leadership is doing, see what the brothers and sisters are doing. Satan sets people inside the congregations for this, ready to say, I'm offended, I'm leaving.

Yet offences are everywhere. Solomon offended, and the whole of Israel was not destroyed; Israel still went on. One man's sin does not destroy everything, which is why we pray and fast for our leadership to stay on course. So take every little thing as a big thing, keep examining yourself, and do not go back to sin, so that the ministry is not blamed.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:19
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” No one can examine you; you examine yourself. “Know ye not your own selves”: you know the evil you are fighting inside, the thoughts you have, the things you do in secret thinking no one sees you. Look in the mirror and ask, self, am I real? Some say they are in the faith, but in secret they are in the midst of all type of evil, giving in again and again to lasciviousness and fornication. If you cannot examine yourself, you are reprobate. Paul prayed “that ye do no evil”, and the same goes for brothers and sisters today.

Then Timothy: “Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” God knows who belongs to him. “And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” Every one of us that calls upon the name of the Lord must depart from iniquity. You brothers should not be adulterers, dealing with prostitutes, dealing with hoes. You sisters should not be sleeping around. No one should be doing schemes and credit card fraud.

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” There are not just vessels of gold here in IUIC. The dishonourable one is faking it in here, here for his own reasons and ulterior motives. So ask yourself: am I real or am I fake? Which vessel are you? Only you alone know, and you have to choose which one you want to be.

Every one of us has demons and thorns we are fighting, so do not act perfect here while Satan has you in a chokehold during the week. We understand you are burning after years of doing it on the regular and now going cold turkey, but come talk to the brothers, go talk to the sisters, and ask for help. Do not let your sins weigh you down and destroy you, because God will judge.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:5-9
precepts.why:
“But the fruit of the Spirit is love”: keeping the commandments. Joy: do you have joy in keeping God's commandments, or are you always sad and depressed? Peace with your wife and with the brothers and sisters, not always arguing and fighting. Longsuffering is patience. Gentleness means being right with your brother; it does not mean you have to be soft and act like a sodomite. Faith is believing what the Bible says. Temperance is self-control, not easily provoked. “against such there is no law”, because you are keeping the law. These fruits develop once the word of God dwells in you.

Peter shows the same fruits: “And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge”. Knowledge means learning the scriptures and learning how to break them down, because we are not going to be on social media all the time. Brothers who will not come around the deacons, bishops and officers to learn the knowledge of God are not going to last in this truth. “And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity”: loving God with all your heart and your brother as yourself. All of these are the fruits your tree must bring forth.

“For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Abound means they stay in you. These things can be in you and then leave you. A brother or sister can be among us six or seven years, growing, the leaves green, and then somebody offends them and all of a sudden they stop bearing fruit.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” So examine yourself: am I bearing good fruit? The Lord does not tell you how long he will be patient. A fig tree that bears no fruit is cut down, and a branch that does not abide in Christ withers and is cast into the fire.

precepts.label: Isaiah 35:4
precepts.why:
Paul thanks God “because that your faith groweth exceedingly, and the charity of every one of you all toward each other aboundeth.” That is what the body needs: brothers and sisters charitable toward each other, with that charity abounding, “in all your persecutions and tribulations that ye endure.” We will suffer for the kingdom of God, and in the suffering we still have to maintain love for our neighbor. It is not about one man; it is about the body of Christ.

Then: “Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you.” The ones troubling the apostles in Thessalonica were Rome. And the Lord Jesus shall be revealed “in flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Christ is coming back for vengeance. That was never taught in church, but it has been in the Bible all along.

Isaiah says the same thing in the Old: “Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” Be strong and do not fear; your God is coming back with vengeance and with the recompense we just read in Thessalonians.

“He will come and save you”: not all people. He is coming to save the Israelites. He is not coming for Christians, not for the Baptists, not for any denomination. And the vengeance falls on those who obey not the gospel, like our people who keep repeating the same evil every year, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year’s, knowing these things are not of God.

thread.text: Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;

precepts.label: Luke 21:24
precepts.why:
“For that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” The day is the day of Christ, when he comes back in flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God. But first there has to be a falling away. What is that? Christ tells us.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword.” The Israelites fell by the sword of the Romans; we fell in 70 AD. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: we fell away into captivity and were dispersed into all nations. That is the falling away. Deuteronomy 28 has to be fulfilled: the day of Christ will not come until Israel first goes into captivity for the evil they did.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles.” So Netanyahu is a Gentile. That is what Christ said. The Jewish people there, the fake Jews, are Gentiles, thus saith the Lord. The ones starving out the Palestinians, bombing them and causing all kinds of ruckus in Iran are not the children of God.

Then “that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.” Esau, the man of sin, has to be revealed to the whole planet, until everybody knows and agrees that this is the son of perdition, the devil on earth. America, with its long list of countries bombed and leaders overthrown, is the most powerful villain: Mystery Babylon the Great.

thread.text: But we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth:

classes.title: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.label: 1 John 2:19
precepts.why:
Paul says, “we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation.” Which of you gives thanks to God every day for the brother or sister sitting next to you? That is the spirit we have to war with from now on: no evil thought of a brother or a sister, but praying and fasting for them, so we may be found faithful in the eyes of God. And it is not a coincidence you are in here. The salvation you are receiving was given to you from the beginning.

How do we know? “They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us.” Some brothers and sisters will come among us who are not of us. If they had been, then no matter what we went through, they would still be with us.

In this body we are going to go through things. This is a hospital; we all need medicine, and the word of God is what heals us. A sister said she left because another sister offended her. How many times have we offended the Lord? We have to build our spirit up so we do not move over every little stupidity.

“But they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” They were not the chosen. The same goes for a spouse: if the unbelieving spouse is pleased to dwell with you, they stay because they love you. When a wife or husband gets up and leaves because you came to the truth, that person never really loved you. So you who are still here, it is no coincidence: you were chosen from the beginning.

precepts.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:1-3
precepts.why:
Paul told Timothy he was persuaded that Christ “is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.” Paul committed his soul, his life, to Christ. What day? Thessalonians explains it: “Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.” That day is the second coming, and all twelve tribes can only gather unto Christ.

“That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.” People were writing letters in Paul’s name saying the second coming had already happened and you missed it. Paul said, I don’t care if you got a letter signed by me, I didn’t write that; that day did not happen yet. Remember in the sixties the FBI would write letters to the Black Panthers and other black organizations in each other’s names. They were doing the same thing with Paul.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” Christ is not going to return until all twelve tribes fall away into captivity. Christians break that down as people leaving Christianity; it is not talking about that crap. It is falling into captivity, as Luke 21:24 says: “they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” All twelve shall fall, and we are still living in the times of the Gentiles.

In Paul’s day, Judah, Benjamin and Levi had not fallen completely; they were still in the land. But 70 AD was soon approaching. So the day Paul committed his soul against has not come yet, and it could not come until all of us fell. And we all fell.

precepts.label: Joel 2:31
precepts.why:
“That day” in Paul’s words to Timothy is the second coming, and Joel shows what kind of day it is: “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” This is a time of war and devastation. When Christ returns, it is going to be a great and terrible day.

Amos says the same: “Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.” We say we can’t wait for the day of the Lord because we don’t really comprehend the magnitude of what is going to happen. You think it is going to be a bright day and Christ will take us all up to the kingdom. It is not that type of a day; it is not that type of a party.

Zephaniah: “The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the Lord: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress.” Don’t think that when the Lord returns we are all going to be standing and cheering. We are going to be running and weeping.

Christ said it in Matthew 24: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days”, which is Jacob’s trouble, “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, because the sky will be black, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles dropping from the sky. The powers of the nations shall be shaken with war. “and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” You think you will be happy, stomping your feet and clapping; the Bible says all the tribes shall mourn, meaning cry bitterly. That is the day Paul was preparing Timothy for, and why he told him to stir up the gift, not fear, and not be ashamed of the afflictions of the gospel.

thread.label: 2 Timothy 4:10,14-16
thread.text: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.

classes.title: War & the Pain of Repentance

precepts.label: Mark 4:16-19
precepts.why:
“For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world.” Demas traveled with Paul and warred with Paul, and he forsook Paul. He saw the looseness of the women: Paul, I’ve got to go, my man, I can’t roll with you no more, I got needs. He let that overcome him. Crescens left for Galatia, Titus for Dalmatia. Mark shows what happened to Paul’s companions, men who were strong in the Lord and in the power of his might. Those guys are some of you guys.

“And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness.” I’m an Israelite, we got history, oh I love it. “And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time.” No root: I don’t study, I don’t addict myself to the ministry, I like my sports, I like my porn, the Bible comes last. So you only endure this gospel for a time.

“afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.” Offended, and you leave. Affliction is things that happen to you; persecution is what happens to you for the word’s sake, because you stand strong in this Bible. That is why Paul told Timothy not to be ashamed of his affliction, to suffer in it with him and stir up the gift within him. Christ lets us know some of us are going to leave this truth because of affliction.

And Satan will test. He asks the Lord, can I test him? Can I test her? The brother with a proclivity for the male gender went to the gym at two in the morning, where the freaks come out at night, found two men in the shower, stood there five whole minutes, and they invited him to join in. If you are struggling, stay out of the gym; do calisthenics at your house. You are trying to fight a spirit; don’t go around spirits like that.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, a piece of the American pie, may not be your thing. But the lust of other things is anything in you that nobody else knows. You may hide it very well, but God knows it is there, Satan knows it is there, and you do too. Satan is not tempting you with a pork chop. He looks into your soul, sees what you are battling with, and asks to tempt you right there.

That is what took Demas, Crescens and Titus, and it is what Paul went through with Alexander the coppersmith, who was in the ministry and turned against it, “for he hath greatly withstood our words.” We have seen the same: men in the gospel who went online to try to tear this down. “At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me.” Christ already prophesied it: “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” In 2018 brothers were dropping like flies, brothers and sisters we broke bread with, who stayed in our homes and knew our families, offended at the gospel and betraying it. Some tried to start Israelite congregations and fell overnight. God is not going to bless your hands after you did so much evil to your brothers and sisters.

thread.label: James 1:14
thread.text: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Mark 7:21
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Lust has nothing to do with love, and love has nothing to do with lust; a lot of us get those two confused. What is a man’s own lust? Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.”

Read on: “Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” Adultery and fornication are sins we battle every day. The spirit of murder you see in this world, and our people fight that demon every day. Covetousness we fight every day, because we lust and covet after these things. Deceit is a demon we fight every day.

These come from within. So the battle is not really from the outside; the thing we lust after is within us, and the battlefield is the mind. A brother can be quiet here but fighting major demons; a sister can be quiet but fighting demons. Quiet does not mean humble. Some are bound with their sin.

And this world feeds it. Everything here is a work of sin. They sell sex everywhere; you think you are watching a movie or a karate flick, and they put that nasty thing in there, and down the line you see how people turn to watching porn. The devil is always there, pushing sin. That is why we have to understand this walk and overcome it: every man is drawn away of his own lust, the evil that comes from within his heart.

thread.label: James 1:25
thread.text: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:8
precepts.why:
Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:10
precepts.why:
The enemy does not sleep, and Revelation shows what he is doing: “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”

Satan isn't sleeping day and night. He is accusing us day and night as we study, trying to accuse us before the Lord. So we don't have time to be idle. We have to keep our minds focused, brothers. Y'all sleep on the devil if you want.

He is at work through this world too. They are trying to change times and laws and make people think that what is immoral is moral. The mind of the sinner says don't judge me and don't snitch, but the one living in sin influences others and destroys others. That is why the laws of God are important.

This is why James 1:25 calls us to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein. The accuser works against us before God day and night, so we must meditate in the law day and night and be doers of the work, so that we are blessed in our deed and the ministry stays blameless.

thread.text: For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:

classes.title: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:4-5
precepts.why:
“For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment”. The angels that sinned are the sons of God in Genesis 6: Seth's line, that messed around with the daughters of men.

“And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”. What was Noah? A preacher of righteousness. So when 1 Peter says “the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing”, what was God doing? He was giving them time, and Noah was preaching repentance the whole while: y'all better repent, the Most High going to destroy this place. They said, you crazy. Look at that dummy building a boat for no reason.

Noah was prophesying all that time because God was longsuffering. He gave them a hundred years to repent, and they did not listen, and only “eight souls were saved by water”.

That is why Peter joins it to Christ, who was “put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit”: a man, not a demigod, brought back to life by the spirit after three days, who “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. Those spirits in prison are his people, us in captivity. As Noah preached righteousness to a world that would not hear, Christ preached to his people in prison, and the longsuffering of God is waiting on us to repent the same way it waited in the days of Noah.

thread.label: 2 Peter 2:14-15
thread.text: Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children:

classes.title: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:20
precepts.why:
Peter describes men “Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls”. In the first videos, what were they touching? Multiple wives, making every excuse in the book, because they are here looking for loopholes to get in the sisters' drawers. Nobody questions them because the souls following them are unstable, not able to go to the book and study to show themselves approved unto God. They “have forsaken the right way”, and the right way is to keep God's commandments: not add to it, not make it up on the spot, not create an alternate reality to fit what you want to do.

So how do you test them? “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” It is everybody's obligation to God in this truth to study to show thyself approved, rightly dividing the word of truth, because you can only know whether they speak according to this word if you study. This stuff is elementary: Matthew 1 and Luke 3 put together. Yet people sit there and let them use five-syllable words and then drop straight stupidity, and nobody asks a question.

These men do not keep the commandments, and that goes for all the other camps and for us too; we are not above it. We must repent and keep the commandments as it is written. And if you run into them on the street, all you have to do is open the Bible. It is kryptonite to them. They don't know the Bible, and their breakdowns make them look foolish.

precepts.label: Proverbs 3:1-7
precepts.why:
These brothers get put on platforms and get a lot of hits, and they don't realize they are being used to defame this truth. The world takes their statements and says that's what all the Israelites think, and the Christians get uppity from those videos and then come in front of us and get embarrassed. A man of understanding would look at who is interviewing him, a guy in a baseball cap with no interest in edifying the truth, and be selective in what he does.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.” Keep the commandments and “So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.” An Israelite elder, a leader, should not look in front of men like he has no understanding. When you go off like that, other brothers in the Israelite community look at you and say, damn, I thought he was a leader, why would he say something so dumb? You're still our brother, but you are an embarrassment. You let them embarrass the Israelites.

Then verse 7: “Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the Lord, and depart from evil.” You are wise in your own eyes. You think you are saying something deep, and you look crazy; you have an unsolved Rubik's cube bouncing around in your cerebellum. That is what forsaking the right way looks like: leaning on your own understanding instead of the commandments.

precepts.label: Sirach 21:14-15
precepts.why:
This is sad. These brothers have lost all wisdom out of their vessel, if they ever obtained it. Look at what we are doing: the secret sauce is keeping the commandments. Just follow the blueprint.

“The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth.” That is why you see foolishness spewing out of their mouths: as was supposed, a whole podcast of it, jargon and foolishness with nothing held inside.

“If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add unto it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.” If a man of no understanding hears the commandments and that he must keep them, it displeases him, and he casts them behind his back. That is what we are looking at right now. He has cast off the law and forsaken the right way, like Peter says, and so all manner of foolishness comes out of these brothers' mouths. That line will not go throughout the earth at all.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 3:8-9
precepts.why:
Only people that don't study get caught up in this foolishness. You can hear people in the crowd agreeing: yeah, oh man. But Paul says: “Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth”. It isn't just him; it is all those that resist the truth, and you will see it over and over.

Why do these dumb doctrines and silly sayings come out? They are “men of corrupt minds”, because they have resisted the truth. It is clear we don't tithe anymore; the temple is not there. It is clear you don't have multiple wives; you read that in 1 Corinthians 7. But they resist the truth, and now their minds are corrupt, and you hear about innie and Audi and all the rest.

They are “reprobate concerning the faith”: these men are not in the faith. They don't believe, and those who get caught up with them are in the same boat. “But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs also was.” They will not go any further. Their folly is being made manifest among all men, and that is why they will have to fix their face.

precepts.label: Titus 1:15-16
precepts.why:
He said if you don't pay these tithes, I'm going to sell myself when Diddy gets out, because these kids have got to eat. For argument's sake, say he needs to raise money for the kids. How does that translate to selling your ass? What's wrong with you? That is a mind that is corrupt.

“Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.” Every time something happens with them, it turns to some weird energy of gayness and sex. It's dark. It's a dark place. Peter called them men with “eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin”, and here it is.

“They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.” If a comment like that were made among us, the congregation would not laugh; we move different. We aren't perfect, but we aren't of that sort. And whoever edited that footage could have cut it if he loved his elder. He is a demon. Brothers, if I ever lose my mind like that, cut the feed and take the mic.

precepts.label: Sirach 20:22
precepts.why:
This one is for everybody who was in that room. Silence is agreement. If you hear that kind of talk and it doesn't compel you to say something, hey, anybody else hear that?, then everybody in that room agreed with it by sitting there and saying nothing. This scripture is for all of you who are scared to speak up.

“There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.” That is what a lot of you are doing: too bashful to speak, accepting the person of your leader, and overthrowing yourselves. Sirach 4 says don't be an underling to a foolish man, and that is what you are doing. There is no Bible open. A man goes to jail for a lot of evil, and your leader says he is about to join him and sell his body. What is edifying about that?

Peter warned of men “beguiling unstable souls” who “have forsaken the right way”. It is time to wake up and realize who is leading you down the road of destruction, separate from them, and do the Father's will. Stop following behind brothers who want to be the new Hebrew Hammer. That is a defiled, nasty negro.

thread.label: 2 Peter 3:1-7
thread.text: This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you; in both which I stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance:

classes.title: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.label: Matthew 24:37-39
precepts.why:
Christ said “This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.” The same generation that was around during Christ's time, guess where they are now? Here. “Heaven and earth shall pass away”: with nuclear fire.

“But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” The exact same people that were ruling during Noah's time will be ruling in this time. The same ignorance Noah faced back then, we are going to face now. The same word he was preaching back then, we are preaching now.

“For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away”. That is Peter's scoffers: in Noah's time they didn't believe. Noah is crazy, building a boat for no reason, him and his crazy sons and wives. Where's your rain at? Where's this judgment coming from? And today they say “all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation”: this is how the world is supposed to be; this ain't captivity, we free.

Peter says the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished, and the heavens and the earth which are now, “by the same word”, the word Noah preached, “are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.” Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech and Noah preached to the wicked of our people mingled among the other people, and the flood came and killed them. Here we are again, preaching to the same wicked sons of God mixed with the same people before the fire comes. It is the exact same thing.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 10:4
precepts.why:
“For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood”: he is the cause. Whose evil was responsible for the earth being flooded? Cain's evil. The heavens that were of old in 2 Peter 3 are Cain's kingdom, the ruling class that was of old, and “the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished”.

The sons of God, Seth's line, went in with Cain's line, and God dealt with them: if you're all for Cain now, I'm going to kill all of you. Then “wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value”: the ark, the little boat the scoffers laughed at, carried Noah through.

Likewise today. Peter says “the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire”. God said, I promised you with the rainbow that I would not flood the earth again. I won't flood it, but I'll burn it. The same cause, the same wicked kingdom ruling, and the same judgment coming, this time by fire, while wisdom directs the course of the righteous who hear the word.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:4-5
precepts.why:
“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people”: out of Babylon. Then, “that ye be not partakers of her sins”: whose sins do we not partake in? Edom's sins. Cain's line handled the music. They were behind all the music back then, and music is very influential, very powerful when it is in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is.

Then Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and brass and iron mean weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing, and it was Cain's blessing too. There is nothing new under the sun.

This is how “every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” Wonderful there means evil; they started to mess around with the daughters of men. And they despised the commandments, which shows the commandments were around back then; that is how Noah knew clean from unclean. The wicked had the music and the weapons then, the same as they do now, and it ended in the flood that destroyed them.

precepts.label: Genesis 4:25-26
precepts.why:
After Cain slew Abel, “Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel.” Seth was Abel's replacement, the replacement of righteousness in the earth.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Ezra says the nations that came out of Adam “despised thy commandments.” When the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again.

Those tribes back then were called the sons of God. Tribes, sons of God: that sounds like the Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; wicked, evil leaders were around back then, and the righteous are around now. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous are always born within the evil.

That line carries straight to the flood. Ezra says God brought the flood on those that dwelt in the world, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That goes back to Shem's line: not Ham's line, not Japheth's line, but Shem's, the line that came down from Seth.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:6
precepts.why:
Ezra says the husbandman's seed perishes “if it come not up, and receive not thy rain in due season; or if there come too much rain, and corrupt it”. The husbandman is the Most High, the seed is the word he sows in us, and the rain is wisdom. Anyone who has planted knows that if too much rain falls on a seed, it does not grow. How can too much rain corrupt a man? Paul shows it: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.”

A novice is somebody new in this truth, a beginner. Some brothers come in and catch on real quick. Why would a novice get lifted up with pride? Because he got too much rain, too much wisdom, and he cannot handle it. He starts getting high-minded, and then he falls into the condemnation of the devil: Satan destroys the seed that is in him. That is what it means when the scripture says too much rain can corrupt the seed. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

That is why the heavy teaching is eased off at times. You may love it when the class goes deep, but too much of that wisdom too fast can corrupt you. The deacons have been learning in this truth for over twenty years. When you see them go into certain things, it comes from years of being watered; nobody woke up one day able to break down the scriptures.

So the Most High gives the rain in its season, moderately, as Joel says, “the former rain moderately”, raising the waters little by little, from the ankles to the knees, so that we can handle it. The seed that receives its rain in due season takes root and bears fruit; the novice who is lifted up with pride perishes like the corrupted seed.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:8
precepts.why:
The eagle is told, “thou hast afflicted the meek, thou hast hurt the peaceable, thou hast loved liars, and destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit, and hast cast down the walls of such as did thee no harm.” The fourth beast was Rome, and America is its extension, ruling with much wicked oppression. America just bombed a school and killed 165 schoolgirls. Wicked as hell. Habakkuk shows what comes back on such a nation.

“Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee”. America has spoiled many nations, and now we see it is America and Israel, Trump and Netanyahu, doing it together. What is the reason? “because of men's blood, and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.”

So the remnant of the people, the nations America has spoiled, shall spoil it. That is what we are watching as Iran answers with missiles the Iron Dome cannot stop, a single missile that turns into eighty. The eagle that cast down the walls of such as did it no harm will have its own walls cast down, because of men's blood.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:7
precepts.why:
Why are these nations mad? Because America has been a tyrant. Jeremiah gives the reason: “Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord's hand, that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunken of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.”

The nations have drunk of her wine, meaning her lies and her philosophies. Therefore the nations are mad: they are angry. Of the eagle it is said, “so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit”, and “thou hast loved liars”, the dirty, grimy lawyers who manipulate the law to do America's bidding. Not every lawyer is wicked, and some of our brothers are lawyers with good intent, but those who twist the law for her are the liars she loves.

Babylon is a golden cup in the Lord's hand. The Lord made her to reign in his world, that the end of their times might come through them, and the nations drunk on her wine are now turning against her. Daniel gives that wine another name.

precepts.label: Daniel 8:25
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says the nations have drunk of Babylon's wine and are mad. Daniel uses another word instead of wine: “And through his policy also he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand; and he shall magnify himself in his heart”.

Through his policy: that is the wine. His policy, his lies and philosophies, are what he gives the nations to drink, and by it he causes craft, deceit, to prosper in his hand. That is the fourth beast of whom Ezra says, “so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit”, that did not judge the earth with truth.

And he magnifies himself in his heart. America in its arrogance kills leaders, bombs in the middle of negotiations, and thinks no one can touch it. But the nations drunk on its policy are mad at it, and oppression unites them.

In the middle of all this war, Isaiah sees the prophets still going out: “Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand”. The banner is the Bible. “Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men”. Since we know what the Lord is going to do, we must persuade our people to change their lives while there is time.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 14:13
thread.text: Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption,

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:9
precepts.why:
“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. Your body is a house; that is the house you live in. Set your life in order, brother, with God's laws, statutes and commandments, and then you can reprove and teach your people. And the Most High has set men over us to do that very work.

“And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.” Our leadership is wise, brothers and sisters; the Lord set them over us for a reason. They teach the people knowledge: how to overcome, how to lead ourselves in the way of righteousness.

Set in order many proverbs: that is what we do when we go over precepts. There are a lot of proverbs we read and don't understand, and leadership puts the puzzle together and sets them in order so you can understand the things of old. “The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright”. They search out what the people need and what they are going through. Sometimes they step on toes, just to wake you up or break the chain you have been fighting with.

So God did not leave us without help. When we go off, he set up brothers and sisters to guide us back home. You can never say God did not send help; the one who ignores it is caught up in stupidity.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra to “comfort such of them as be in trouble”, and that comfort comes out of the scriptures: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” That which was written was upright, and we have to understand it and follow it. That's the pattern.

That is where our hope comes from. When we look at the history of our forefathers, whatever they went through, brothers and sisters, is what we are going to go through, so we are not shocked at what is going on. And it is the same in the body: the Captain went through it, I can go through it; the Deacon went through it, I can go through it; the sister went through it, I can go through it. That is the comfort that keeps us from giving up.

So don't give up. No matter what, stand up. This profession, made before many witnesses, is all we have; some of us have twenty years and more in this truth. Where can we go? This is our life. Don't let Satan take it away from you, and don't give it up for Babylon's money; Babylon will destroy your soul. Set your house in order, revive your own soul first, and then revive your people.

precepts.label: Joel 3:1-2
precepts.why:
Ezra's vision says, “Behold, saith God, I will call together all the kings of the earth to reverence me, which are from the rising of the sun, from the south, from the east, and Libanus; to turn themselves one against another, and repay the things that they have done to them.” From the south, the Arab nations; from the east, China and India. Joel is the precept to it.

“For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel”. I will gather all nations: that is the calling together of all the kings of the earth in 2 Esdras 15.

The valley of Jehoshaphat is in the Middle East. So what do we see right now? More and more nations are putting their attention on the Middle East, and right now the focus is America and Iran. There the Lord is going to plead with the nations for his people, his heritage Israel, whom they scattered among the nations.

This is what the prophecies say; the vision is for an appointed time, and at the end it shall speak and not lie. So when we see this war, we are supposed to rejoice and increase our faith. We are drawing closer to Christ's return, so we have to draw closer to each other, fellowship more, fast and pray more.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:17
precepts.why:
Trump said of the war with Iran that they are doing this not for now, but for the future. Why would he say that? Go to the Bible and see what it says about Iran, the Medes, in the future: “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.”

America knows the prophecy says Iran is going to be stirred up against them. They do not need money and they do not want money; they want vengeance. That is why America has been striking at Iran for years: the drone strike that killed Soleimani in 2020, who was uniting the Arabs, the Houthis, Hamas and Hezbollah; the strikes on the nuclear sites; the death of the Supreme Leader, whom the Muslim world regarded like the Pope; a president killed in a so-called helicopter accident; a bomb dropped in the middle of negotiations. You cannot trust the white man.

But oppression unites. In their arrogance they are only making Iran more powerful, and now they view the dead as martyrs. Iran's hypersonic missiles, the Fattah 2, change course in mid-flight and get through the Iron Dome despite navy ships and bases in Iraq and Jordan shooting them down. This is the technology our forefathers saw in vision, the Lord's technology.

Our power is not missiles or guns; our power is the word of God. We foretell these things, and when the people see them happen, they will respect this Bible even more. As Paul says, “it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.” The Lord will use the teaching of the Bible to bring America down.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:1
precepts.why:
The Lord says to them who keep his commandments and precepts, “let not your sins weigh you down.” Sin feels good. The pleasure comes, and once the pleasure is gone the guilt rolls in, and you feel like crap. After a while it becomes a burden, and it shows on you. Many of us came into the school guilty of things too shameful to confess, and some are still doing them. When you come forward and confess, you feel that weight lifted off: thank God.

Paul uses the same picture: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.” Lay aside every weight. Your sins of character are weights.

If you run a race carrying weights, can you run fast? No. You can still be in the race, but you either keep adding weight until you come in last and never cross the finish line, or you take the weights off. One weight off and you feel lighter; another off and you are faster. You were in third, now second, now first.

Some of y’all say, I’m good back here, I’ll just walk. Meanwhile you are on a timer, and time at the end is running out. A race is won by the time you run. If you are walking in a race, you are not winning at all, by no account.

That is why we lay aside every weight: the sins that so easily beset us are what hold us back. It is what 2 Esdras means: do not let your sins weigh you down.

precepts.label: Psalms 94:16
precepts.why:
The Lord God says, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” And: “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes.” Brothers give up their position because of the affliction, the little tribulation, or because of their bills, two hundred-some thousand dollars of debt. How could you be that stupid, that ignorant? We all have bills. That is all you have. Their sin is wearing them down so much, and they are so covered with it that they cannot see the brotherhood right in front of them.

David asks the question every one of us has to answer: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” You have to stand up.

The evildoers are where we are today. Taking a man out of his country and bringing him back to America: the same America that pushes democracy, when democracy put him there, kidnaps him and charges him with unjust judgment. Is that just, or wicked? If it is hard for you to see that America is evil, it is because you are evil yourself. Everything here is a work of iniquity; they push sin everywhere, even in a little karate flick.

Christ said, “I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world.” Have the word of God and the world will hate you, and your family will hate you. “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.” He left us in the world because we have a path to go through: from Adam until now it has been good against evil, and our job is to stand for what is right. “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The stony ground “immediately receive it with gladness”, but has no root, and when affliction arises “immediately they are offended.” What have you given for this truth? Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are the children of Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you are alive, you still have it. So who will rise up and stand? Do not let your sins weigh you down.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:3
precepts.why:
Sirach says “I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.” With a war between America and Iran unfolding and many prophecies being fulfilled, we look at what the Bible says about prophecy itself.

“Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand.” Blessed is he that reads and hears, and keeps the things written therein. What is written in the scriptures? The laws of the Most High God.

So the blessing is not only in reading the prophecy but in keeping the law. We are blessed when we read and keep the things written in the law, because the time is at hand, and the doctrine poured out as prophecy was left for all ages, including ours.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:19-21
precepts.why:
“I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.” Peter says, “We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed”. Take heed to do what the scriptures say. The Most High called us into this truth, so we have to take heed.

“as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place. That is why Christ said, let your light so shine before men. We have to be that example for our people, to win them over into the faith. Whether you are in DC, New Orleans, California or the UK, the Most High chose us, and through our example we have to win our people over.

“Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” Prophecy is the foretelling of future events in the Bible, and it did not come by the will of man. Holy men of God, holy black men, holy Hispanic men, spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. That is the light sent forth afar off.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:1-5
precepts.why:
“Behold, speak thou in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, which I will put in thy mouth, saith the Lord”. Speak in the ears of my people. That is why in Ezekiel he said not to go to a people of a strange speech: we have to deal with our people.

“And cause them to be written in paper: for they are faithful and true.” Everything written in the Bible is faithful and true.

“Fear not the imaginations against thee, let not the incredulity of them trouble thee, that speak against thee. For all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness.” Do not fear what the nations are going to do to us for teaching against America and against governments. The Bible says do not fear.

“Behold, saith the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” The Most High says he is going to bring judgment upon the world. That is the doctrine Sirach says was poured out as prophecy and left to all ages, and we do not labour for ourselves only: we speak it in the ears of our people.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 15:7-8
precepts.why:
When we teach the Bible and bring out the prophecy, in the street or in classes, what are these scriptures supposed to do for our people? The prophet told King Asa: “Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.” The days we are living in now are not the time for us to be weak.

“And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim”. When Asa heard the words of the prophecy, he took courage.

That is what prophecy is supposed to do for us: give us the courage to let go of our idols and our secret sins. We are seeing prophecy unravel right before our eyes: Iran and Israel going to war, and now America getting involved. It was a rumor and talk for years, and now we see it unfold. That means more Israelites are repenting, and more of our brothers and our people are waking up. That is the doctrine poured out as prophecy, laboured for all them that seek wisdom.

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:15-16
precepts.why:
Baruch says, “Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God”, and “unto us and to our fathers open shame, as appeareth this day.” Here in America we have open shame, because we departed from our God and refuse to come back and repent. Lamentations shows what that open shame looks like.

“All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem.” All the other nations pass by and clap their hands at us. They are happy we are thrown down, happy we are not exalted, happy we are at the bottom.

“Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” Everybody knows we are the perfection of beauty: our skin, our hair, our lips, our eyes. Flip the coin and look at Esau, wrinkled and dried up with skin cancer, twenty years old looking forty. And we are the joy of the whole earth: even in the lowest state we are in, everything we do, everybody follows.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth.” Starting with Edom on down. You go in the Chinese hair store, the nail shop, the gas station, the Arab store, the East Indian store, and they open their mouth against you; they don’t give a damn about you. “They say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.” We don’t have a community, only neighborhoods, and in our own neighborhoods they own everything and we are the consumers. This is the day they hoped for, to see us break our laws and fall.

But now the Lord is waking his prophets back up to get his people back in order, to turn this place upside down, so we can have rulership on this earth again in righteousness.

classes.title: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “Thou therefore, O Lord, that art the God of the just, hast not appointed repentance to the just.” Obviously: if you are just, you have nothing to repent from. But what makes you just?

Paul answers it: “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The law is holy, and the commandment is holy, just and good. When you are applying it, that is what makes you just. That is what makes you good: the law and the commandment.

So the God of the just is the God of those who keep the commandments, “as to Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, which have not sinned against thee.” They kept God’s laws. Repentance was not appointed for them.

“But thou hast appointed repentance unto me that am a sinner.” Manasseh knew he was not just. He had broken the holy, just and good commandment on every count, and his only hope was the repentance the Lord appoints unto sinners.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 1:9-11
precepts.why:
Manasseh says the God of the just “hast not appointed repentance to the just.” Paul says the same exact thing: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient.” The law is not made for a righteous man, just as repentance is not appointed for the just.

It is made “for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”, that is homosexuality, “for menstealers”, child traffickers, “for liars, for perjured persons”, liars under oath before the judge, “and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine”, anything not listed.

“According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.” The law is in accordance with the gospel. You cannot have one without the other.

That list is Manasseh. Under the law of Moses he was condemned on all accounts: he killed babies, he was an idolater and a murderer, he shed the blood of children from one end of Jerusalem to the other, and he was steeped in every evil. He was America, but a king; Epstein, but a king; King Diddy Manasseh. There was no animal he could sacrifice. He was a king worthy of death, and his mindset was, I’m the king, I do what I want. The Lord said, you’re the king? Cool, and threw him in prison.

Yet the Lord appointed repentance unto him, and let him live as an example to us in this time. Most kings and celebrities with that status will not repent. When you are rich you become your own god; they literally call them idols. Oprah said on air she does not respect a jealous God. But Manasseh humbled himself, and that is the lesson.

precepts.label: Luke 18:9-14
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “I am not worthy to behold and see the height of heaven for the multitude of mine iniquities.” Many of us think this. Christ gives a parable about that very man, spoken “unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others.” Those who were righteous in their own eyes and despised everybody else were the Pharisees: I'm more righteous than you, you're wicked.

“Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.” The publican was a tax collector, and they were praying in the same place. The Pharisee thanked God he was “not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican”, not like this dude next to him, and bragged, “I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.”

“And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven.” Why? Because he felt unworthy, the same as Manasseh, who could not behold the height of heaven. He “smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner”: the same thing Manasseh said in his prayer, my sins are a multitude.

Christ's judgment: “this man went down to his house justified rather than the other.” The sinner who asked for mercy went home justified; the one who called himself righteous did not. “for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased”: that is what Manasseh did in the beginning, exalting himself, and he was brought down to a low condition, locked up and imprisoned. “and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted”: that is Manasseh later on, after he humbled himself.

So humble yourself and you will be exalted. Exalt yourself and you will be humbled, and you are not going to like that humbling either.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
Manasseh confesses, “I did not thy will, neither kept I thy commandments.” Those two go together, because the Lord's will is his commandments. David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

To do God's will is to have his law in your heart. The laws of God are the will of God; God's will is his laws. So when Manasseh says he did not God's will, he is saying the same thing twice: he did not keep the commandments. Not doing the will of God is not some mystery feeling; it is breaking his law.

That is why Manasseh goes straight on to say, “I have set up abominations, and have multiplied offences.” He had provoked the Lord's wrath and done evil before him, and he was bowed down with iron bands, locked up with no release. A man who delights to do God's will keeps the law within his heart; Manasseh had to come to that by being humbled, bowing the knee of his heart and acknowledging his iniquity.
